headline: Every Saudi giga-project sends a delivery chief to Riyadh at the end of September
deck: ROSHN, Diriyah, Red Sea Global, NEOM, AlUla, King Salman Park, New Murabba, Qiddiya and Expo 2030 all appear on a single published agenda.
excerpt: MEED's Saudi Mega Projects gathers delivery executives from almost every Saudi giga-project at ROSHN's Riyadh venue from 28 September, with around 75 speakers on a published agenda.
content:
Saudi Mega Projects runs at The Venue by ROSHN in Riyadh from 28 September under the theme of turning vision into value, organised by MEED with ROSHN as host partner and free to attend. Unlike most events in the Saudi September calendar, it has published a full session-by-session agenda and a speaker list running to roughly seventy-five names.

The roster is what makes it significant. Charles Biele, group chief operating officer at ROSHN, and Oussama Kabbani, group chief development officer, appear for the host. Diriyah sends Matthew Boot as chief projects officer and Josep Forroll as chief development strategy officer. Expo 2030 Riyadh sends Eng Murad AlSayed as chief delivery officer. Fabien Toscano appears as chief executive of AlUla Development Company, Dale Chadwick as chief development officer of the King Salman Park Foundation, Raymond Rice for New Murabba, Muhammed Alqahtani as executive vice president for delivery at Sports Boulevard, and Ben Edwards and Neal Coote for Red Sea Global. Talal Almaiman attends as chief executive of Kingdom Holding.

Between them, the represented programmes cover ROSHN, Diriyah, Red Sea Global, NEOM including Trojena and Oxagon, AlUla, King Salman Park, New Murabba, Sports Boulevard, Soudah Peaks, Qiddiya, Expo 2030 and Riyadh Metro. It is difficult to think of a Saudi development programme of consequence that is not on that list.

The delivery-side seniority is the useful detail. Chief projects officers and delivery executives are the people who know which packages are out to tender, which have slipped and what the sequencing constraints actually are — information contractors and suppliers ordinarily assemble from fragments. Terrence Fetters attends as vice president for Riyadh Metro at Parsons and Belal Deiranieh as chief executive of SYSTRA Arabia, giving the consultant perspective, with Iain Thomson of Bechtel on Jubail and Ras Al-Khair.

The attending partner list points at where the commercial interest sits: Jotun, Nesma and Partners, El Seif, Henkel Polybit, KEO, Pinsent Masons, Sesco Steel and Favelle Favco — coatings, contractors, engineering, law and heavy lifting equipment. Henkel Polybit and Jotun have both featured in this publication's coverage of the Saudi construction chemicals market.

MEED puts around $130bn of giga-project work already awarded and roughly $200bn currently in the market. Those are the organiser's figures and should be attributed as such.

One discrepancy is worth resolving before travel. The published agenda runs across four day-blocks ending 1 October, while the headline dates are given as 28 to 30 September. Anyone booking should confirm the final day with the organiser.
